prompt: Name TWO measures of **variability** for a data set (separate with a comma).
hint: Variability describes how spread out the data values are, not where they are centered.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Think about a simple list such as $1, 5, 9$. Which numbers could you report to describe how spread out it is?
Variability describes how spread out the data values are, not where they are centered.
Think of the measures found by subtracting: largest minus smallest, and $Q_3 - Q_1$. A third one averages the distances from the mean. Name any two.
Two measures of variability are the range and the IQR (the MAD would also count).

explanation: A measure of variability tells how spread out the values of a data set are.
The range is the largest value minus the smallest, and the IQR (interquartile range) is $Q_3 - Q_1$.
The MAD (mean absolute deviation) is the average distance of the values from the mean.
Any two of these work, so one correct answer is range, IQR.
